ArXiv cs.AI.title: Who May Overrule the Agent? Evidence-Gated Authority in LLM Review Institutions
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.05390v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-agent language-model systems often add a reviewer to improve an upstream agent's decision. Yet a reviewer can both repair errors and replace decisions that were already correct. We study this as a problem of institutional jurisdiction: conditional on the same proposal, task information, model, and review output, when is the reviewer authorized to make its recommendation binding? ArXiv cs.AI.title: Agent Harness Awareness: Turning Verified Telemetry into Operational Control for Tool-Using Agents
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.05391v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tool descriptions tell an agent what an action can do, but they do not necessarily reveal whether that action is healthy or suitable at the moment of use. Execution harnesses often possess this information through monitors, traces, and recent failures while the model choosing the next action does not. We call this gap operational blindness. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Uncertainty-Aware Resource Orchestration for Agentic AI Systems
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.05392v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems powered by large language models (LLMs) execute as autonomous multi-step pipelines that dynamically invoke tools, integrate observations into memory, and iterate until a task is resolved or a resource budget is exhausted. Unlike classical workflows with fixed graphs, the aggregate compute, bandwidth, and end-to-end latency demands of such pipelines are unknown at dispatch time: they emerge at runtime from intermediate observations and stochastic token sampling, yielding heavy-tailed, multi-modal rando

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Challenge-Aware Knowledge Recruitment with Meta-Agent Supervision for Medical Multi-Agent Reasoning
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.05393v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models perform strongly on standard medical QA but degrade on harder reasoning tasks, where multi-agent debate often fails to beat strong single-model prompting. We argue that a key limitation is that existing systems select experts and retrieve knowledge from the question alone, rather than from gaps that emerge during reasoning. We propose challenge-aware adaptive recruitment: an external CHALLENGER inspects the evolving reasoning trace and identifies specific factual or expertise gaps. ArXiv cs.AI.title: A Feasibility Condition for Confidence-Gated Tiered LLM Inference
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.05394v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tiered inference distributes large language model computation across a hierarchy of devices, from on-device and edge hardware to the datacenter, and is increasingly offered as the route to cheaper, lower-latency, and more private serving. Most such systems orchestrate frozen model checkpoints, and most decide what to resolve locally and what to escalate using a confidence signal produced by a forward-deployed model. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Towards Robust Long-Lived Agents: Benchmarking Experience Lifecycles in Evolving Environments
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.05450v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As agents become more capable, they are moving beyond one-off tasks toward sustained assistance across successive user goals. Such assistance requires agents to discover how unfamiliar environments work, reuse what they learn across tasks, and keep that experience current as environments evolve. Existing benchmarks increasingly study experience reuse and adaptation, but provide limited insight into which parts of accumulated experience agents revise, retain, or lose. To address this gap, we introduce ReScopeBench, a benchmark for the experience

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Can Large Language Models Review the Scientific Literature? A Test Against a 102-Article Benchmark
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.05459v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support scientific literature reviews, yet evaluations often examine individual tasks rather than the review process as a whole. We assess six AI tools across four stages: finding relevant articles, interpreting them, synthesizing across them, and proposing future research. The benchmark is a published review of the Spanish plume weather pattern and its 102-article corpus.

ArXiv cs.AI.title: SlackBench: Benchmarking Agents on Collaborative Projects Grounded in Real Code Repositories
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.05512v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI Agents are becoming digital coworkers that can browse the web, write code, run experiments, and assist humans over extended horizons. Yet existing benchmarks fall short of real knowledge work: many rely on synthetic data or isolated tasks, missing the complex, multi-party dynamics of collaborative projects, where critical information is scattered across conversations, code, and evolving decisions. Even simple workplace questions may require locating relevant channels and direct messages, recovering context from long discussions, inspecting re

ArXiv cs.AI.title: MA-SafeDiffuser: Safe Multi-Agent Planning with Diffusion Probabilistic Models
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.05524v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose MA-SafeDiffuser, a multi-agent extension of SafeDiffuser that equips diffusion-based trajectory planners with finite-time diffusion invariance guarantees for joint-agent safety specifications. Building on the single-agent construction that embeds control barrier function (CBF) constraints into reverse-diffusion updates, we: (i) formalize joint safe sets as intersections of per-agent and pairwise barrier sets; (ii) derive centralized and decentralized (communication-aware) constrained denoising procedures with provable invariance under

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Towards Efficient Whole Page Ranking with One-Pass Inference
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.05542v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Whole-page ranking jointly optimizes advertisements and organic content to balance business outcomes and user engagement under complex layout and business constraints. Existing non-autoregressive (NAR) approaches enable efficient page generation but typically score candidate items independently of previously selected items, limiting their ability to capture order-dependent interactions. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Iterated creation, grading, and revision of data science projects by language models
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.05548v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We evaluate the extent to which agentic AI models can complete an end-to-end data science project, and how this improves with feedback. A 'writer' model with specific tools creates a complete data science project including downloading, cleaning, and analyzing a dataset, and writing a short paper about it. The project is executed and a 'grader' model evaluates it. The writer can then revise its submission, and this repeats for a total of three rounds. We consider seven models from five developers: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, and Z.AI. Ea

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Whose Transparency is it Anyway? Understanding Generative AI Transparency Needs and Gaps Across Stakeholders
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.05549v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Transparency has become a central principle in AI governance, yet there is little agreement about what transparency means, for whom, and in what contexts. Drawing on interpretive flexibility within the Social Construction of Technology, this paper examines how different stakeholders understand and experience transparency in generative AI. ArXiv cs.AI.title: VirtualTrialHarness: Coordinating Agentic Operationalization of Virtual Trial Protocols Across Complex Clinical Schemas
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.05551v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Virtual trials use routinely collected clinical data to evaluate treatment strategies, but translating a study protocol into an executable analysis requires determining how clinical concepts and study requirements should be represented in the available data and applied consistently across the workflow. These decisions depend on local data representations and operational conventions and can involve source selection, patient and encounter identity, linkage, and temporal interpretation. ArXiv cs.AI.title: AGORA: Reliability-Aware Aggregation of LLM Judges via Item-Response Theory
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.05556v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-as-a-judge is a common substitute for costly human evaluation, and aggregating several judges is the standard remedy for any single judge's bias. Judge pools mix judges of very different reliability, while the human-labeled sets that validate them hold a few hundred items or fewer. In this regime the per-item mean weights weak judges as heavily as strong ones, and confusion-table models such as Dawid-Skene must estimate a per-judge error table from too few items. We propose AGORA (Aggregation Of Reliability-weighted Assessments), an item-res

ArXiv cs.AI.title: BrainBind: Bridging Synchronized EEG and fMRI through Long-Form Naturalistic Video Representations
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.05581v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Real-world vision is dynamic and scene-rich, while EEG and fMRI resolve it at complementary temporal and spatial scales. Most neural decoding systems, however, align one modality in isolation and mostly against static images or short clips. We study the synchronized case: EEG and fMRI are recorded during the same long-form naturalistic viewing, giving a shared stimulus but also recurring narrative context and many semantically similar candidates. We present BrainBind, a framework that maps synchronized EEG and fMRI into frozen long-form video em

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Latent Cluster Separation as a Regularizer for Lifelong Anomaly Detection
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03652v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Lifelong (continual) anomaly detection systems must learn a sequence of tasks without forgetting how to recognize anomaly types seen earlier -- a property known as backward transfer. A common way to try to improve backward transfer is to reshape a model's internal representation around learnable concept centroids, typically coupled with a new way of scoring anomalies based on distance to those centroids. Because these two design choices are usually introduced together, it is unclear which one is actually responsible for any performance gain. In

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Four Extensions of the Universal Law of Robustness: Log-Concave Covariates, Heterogeneous Mixtures, Vector-Valued Predictors, and Markovian Data
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03653v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Bubeck and Sellke's universal law of robustness says that fitting $n$ noisy samples below the noise level with a class of $p$ real parameters forces a Lipschitz constant of order $\sqrt{nd/p}$, when the covariate distribution on $\mathbb{R}^d$ is isoperimetric: smooth interpolation costs a factor $d$ of overparametrization. Its hypotheses are Gaussian-type concentration, a homogeneous covariate law, scalar outputs, and independent samples; we relax each one. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03654v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Cardiac auscultation traditionally detects the presence of a heart murmur, but clinicians further characterize it by timing, shape, pitch, quality, and grade. Most automatic phonocardiogram analysis systems stop at binary detection and do not estimate this richer description. In this work, we formulate automatic murmur characterization as five patient-level classification tasks and compare three multi-spot strategies on recordings from the aortic, pulmonary, mitral, and tricuspid auscultation locations. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03655v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models often spread a concept across many internal dimensions, making their features difficult to interpret. Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) recover clearer features after training. We ask whether models can instead learn interpretable output coordinates directly. We introduce Mixture of Wide Experts (MoWE), a sparse feed-forward layer in which selected experts read the full representation but write to fixed, disjoint output coordinates. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03656v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Why do some of the world's most powerful Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems still struggle to reason about cause and effect? Causal discovery, the ability to discern the underlying drivers of a system, is fundamental to scientific inquiry and has traditionally relied on structured data and statistical methods. Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have been explored as an alternative paradigm for causal inference, leveraging their broad knowledge and reasoning capabilities. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Learning Directional Randers Geometry for Latent-Space Exploration
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03675v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deep neural networks extract powerful latent representations from images, enabling fast and efficient downstream analysis. However, these latent spaces lack explicit geometric structure, leading to possibly poor interpolation fidelity and misleading extrapolation. Latent interpolation techniques assume symmetric transition costs which are often not the case for real world data. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Does the Trust Boundary Hold over Time? A Long-Horizon Benchmark for Receiver-Directed Federated Learning
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03724v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In receiver-directed federated learning, each site draws a trust boundary. For every source and model component it judges, on its own data, whether the transfer helps (admit), harms (reject) or cannot yet be told (abstain). We ask whether this boundary holds over hundreds of rounds. Our benchmark has a federation of thirteen semi-synthetic sites, an exact oracle for every evaluated transfer, paired seeds, an attack protocol, fourteen methods over 600 rounds and Qwen3-1.7B LoRA sites over 500. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03727v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Benchmarks built from model hubs combine interaction data, knowledge graphs (KGs) and resource documentation, but valid files do not ensure that these artifacts describe the same objects. Treating the release as a data product, we audit HuggingBench (SIGIR 2025), a benchmark for recommending Hugging Face resources, through data validation, a replication of its eleven recommendation methods and controlled experiments with three training seeds. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Minimal Superior Penalties: Characterising and Calibrating Decision-Aware Proper Scoring Rules
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03734v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Training a classifier means letting a validation metric decide which model is kept and when training stops. A natural requirement on that metric is superiority: every correctly classified forecast should score better than every incorrectly classified one, however close the underlying probabilities are. Neither the Brier score nor the logarithmic score satisfies this on its own. We show that superiority is governed by the separation between two endpoints -- the supremum of the score on correct predictions and the infimum on incorrect predictions

ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03737v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Extracting semantically meaningful staypoints from raw trajectory streams is a foundational prerequisite for mobility analytics. However, real-world trajectory data is frequently degraded by severe spatial noise and protracted temporal dropouts. Classic threshold-based extraction methods, such as the widely adopted sliding-window algorithm, are highly sensitive to these anomalies, routinely fracturing continuous stationary episodes into disjointed fragments. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03738v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accurate forecasting and temporal downscaling of solar irradiance is critical for reliable renewable energy integration and grid management. Traditional methods often struggle to capture rapid irradiance variability. In this work, we develop a Transformer-based architecture for simultaneous forecasting and temporal downscaling. The model takes input data at arbitrary resolutions and generates outputs at any resolutions represented within the training data, leveraging both global and local contextual information. ArXiv cs.LG.title: CaRe-KT: Continuity-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Knowledge Tracing
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03744v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Knowledge tracing (KT) estimates learners' evolving knowledge states from interaction histories to support adaptive learning. Retrieval-augmented KT improves these estimates using cross-learner behavioral evidence, but existing approaches typically separate evidence retrieval from downstream prediction. This creates a retrieval-inference alignment gap because evidence relevance varies with the learner's evolving state and prediction context. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03755v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Financial workflows need fast, calibrated, auditable decisions, not just generated text. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Language Models Can Benefit from Domain-Specific Inductive Biases
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03756v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models are typically trained with a single choice of architecture on diverse domains and data sources. Modern transformers have been extensively refined for such general-purpose learning, but are they equally effective across different subsets of the pretraining data? We investigate this question by training small language models from scratch on representative subsets of pretraining data such as web text, code, and mathematics. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.03764v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Diffusion models trained on distinct datasets can produce highly similar samples when prompted with the same noise input, suggesting that they learn a generalized data distribution. We investigate the role of noise injected during the sampling process, and show that it plays an important role in making or breaking this strong generalization effect.
